title: Orders & Execution
intro: This level covers the path of an order from instruction to execution across EU and US venues: order types, execution routes, best execution, costs, FIX messages and contract notes. It also covers integrals, Taylor approximations and the normal and lognormal distributions as applied to financial problems.

modules.title: Order types & lifecycle
modules.hook: Market, limit, stop and other order types, time-in-force instructions, and the states an order passes through from entry to fill, cancel or expiry.

units.title: Anatomy of an order: market, limit, marketable limit
objectives: Learner can list the mandatory fields of an equity order and say which are optional
Learner can predict the fill of a market vs a limit order against a given book
Learner can explain why a marketable limit order is the retail default
key_concepts: side, instrument (ISIN + MIC), quantity, price, TIF

exercises.task: Compute average fill price and total cost of a market order walking a 3-level book
Pick the outcome of a limit order given a book snapshot
Complete a description of an order ticket (side, MIC, limit, TIF)
Sort order attributes into 'client instruction' vs 'system-assigned'

units.title: Conditional and hidden-liquidity order types
objectives: Learner can distinguish stop, stop-limit and trailing-stop triggers and their risks
Learner can explain iceberg, pegged and minimum-quantity orders and when a PM would use each
Learner can choose an order type for a stated client goal
units.worked_example: A client holds Eni at 14.80 and enters a sell stop at 14.20. The stock gaps to 13.90 at the open; the stop triggers and becomes a market order filled around 13.90, not 14.20 - the order type protects the trigger, not the price.

exercises.task: Which order type fits this client goal (protect gains, hide size, track the mid)?
Compute realised price of a triggered stop after a gap
Match order types to their trigger/visibility behaviour
Place trigger, activation and fills for a trailing stop on a price path

units.title: Time in force and order validity
objectives: Learner can apply DAY, GTC, GTD, IOC, FOK and auction-only validity rules to a scenario
Learner can explain how venue rules cap GTC lifetime and what happens at corporate actions
Learner can say which TIFs are market-wide vs broker-managed
units.worked_example: A GTC limit buy at 50.00 is placed on Friday. On Monday the stock goes ex-dividend by 1.20; many venues cancel or adjust resting orders, while some brokers re-price. The learner decides which behaviour the client agreement states.

exercises.task: Which TIF produces a partial fill that is then cancelled (IOC) vs no fill at all (FOK)?
Fill in expiry rules for DAY/GTD/GTC for a given venue
Order the events of a GTD order across three trading days with an ex-date
Spot the invalid TIF/order-type combination on an order ticket

units.title: The order lifecycle and its states
objectives: Learner can trace an order from receipt to terminal state naming each state change
Learner can distinguish cancel, replace, reject, expire and done-for-day
Learner can reconcile order quantity with CumQty and LeavesQty
key_concepts: new / pending new / partially filled / filled
units.worked_example: Order to sell 100,000 shares: fills of 20,000 @25.10, 35,000 @25.08 and 15,000 @25.12 leave 30,000; the PM replaces the limit and the replace is rejected because the order is mid-fill. CumQty 70,000, AvgPx 25.0943.

exercises.task: Sequence the states of an order that is partially filled, amended, then cancelled
Compute CumQty, LeavesQty and average price after a series of fills
Name the resulting state after a cancel request races against a fill
Complete an execution blotter row by row

sources.ref: Ch. on trade lifecycle and order management

units.title: Care, DMA and algos; OMS, EMS and smart routing
objectives: Learner can explain the difference between care, DMA, sponsored access and algorithmic orders
Learner can draw the OMS-EMS-broker-venue chain and say where each control sits
Learner can match a trading objective to an algo family
key_concepts: algo families: VWAP, TWAP, POV, IS, dark seekers
units.worked_example: A PM wants to sell 1.5m shares equal to 25% of ADV. She sends it 'care' to the desk who slice it with a POV 15% algo through the broker's SOR; a small tail goes DMA to a dark midpoint pool.

exercises.task: Match workflow terms (care, DMA, algo, SOR) to their definitions
Order the system chain for a DMA order from PM to venue
Choose the algo for a stated objective and urgency
Sort controls into pre-trade, at-trade and post-trade

units.title: Allocation, aggregation and block trades
objectives: Learner can allocate a filled block across accounts pro-rata and by average price
Learner can explain the fairness principle behind aggregation and allocation
Learner can distinguish a block, a large-in-scale order and a cross
units.worked_example: A PM buys 90,000 shares for three funds (A 50k, B 30k, C 10k) and the broker fills 81,000 at VWAP 12.304. Pro-rata gives A 45,000, B 27,000, C 9,000 all at 12.304; the policy says odd lots go to the largest fund.

exercises.task: Allocate a partial fill pro-rata with lot rounding and compute each account's cost
Complete an allocation sheet with average price and commission split
Judge whether a post-trade reallocation breaches the allocation policy
Spot the unfair allocation (cherry-picking) in a sheet

sources.ref: Arts 67-70 (client order handling, aggregation and allocation)
Ch. on trade capture and allocation

units.title: Order handling duties, timestamps and record-keeping
objectives: Learner can list the MiFID II duties on handling client orders and the matching FINRA/SEC duties
Learner can state what must be recorded for each order and for how long
Learner can spot an order-handling breach in a case
units.worked_example: A limit order is received at 10:02:15.348 UTC and entered at 10:05:40 after manual rekeying; a regulator asks why the stamp differs from the client's call recording by three minutes - the learner identifies the record-keeping gap.

exercises.task: Identify which duty a given conduct breaches
Spot missing fields in an order record (timestamp, client ID, decision-maker)
Fill retention periods and clock tolerances
Optional: write a one-page order-handling policy for a small broker

minigame.name: Order Book
minigame.variant: Level 1: submit market/limit/stop orders against a live book, watch fills, partials and the spread

modules.unit_test: End-of-module test: order types, TIF, state transitions, partial-fill arithmetic, allocation and order-handling duties.
modules.jurisdiction_notes: EU first (MiFID II/MiFIR order handling); US comparison via Reg NMS/FINRA 4511 and Rule 15c3-5.

modules.title: Venues & market structure
modules.hook: Regulated markets, MTFs, systematic internalisers and dark pools, the opening, continuous and closing phases, and how venue choice depends on order type and size.

units.title: The venue taxonomy: RM, MTF, OTF, SI, OTC
objectives: Learner can classify a venue by MiFID II category and state its key rules
Learner can say who may operate each venue type and what instruments it can list
Learner can map real EU venues to their category
units.worked_example: Euronext Milan is a regulated market, Turquoise is an MTF, Tradeweb's EU bond venue is an MTF, a bank's broker-crossing network is an OTF only for non-equity, and a bank quoting bilaterally in Eni under SI rules is an SI.

exercises.task: Match venue names to MiFID II categories
Sort features (discretion, firm quotes, listing, public order book) into venue types
Choose the correct execution venue definition for a scenario

units.title: Order-driven markets: books, auctions and price-time priority
objectives: Learner can run an opening or closing auction and derive the uncrossing price
Learner can apply price-time priority and pro-rata matching to a stream of orders
Learner can explain volatility interruptions and circuit breakers
key_concepts: auction uncrossing price (max volume, min imbalance)
units.worked_example: Pre-open orders: buys 4,000@10.05, 3,000@10.04, 5,000@10.02; sells 3,500@10.01, 4,000@10.03, 6,000@10.06. Max-volume price 10.03-10.04 -> 7,000 matches at the rule-determined price; the learner applies the tie-break.

exercises.task: Compute the auction uncrossing price and executed volume
Sequence matches for a live book under price-time priority
Fill a cumulative supply/demand table for an auction
Predict venue behaviour on a price move that triggers a volatility pause

sources.ref: Chapters on auctions and order books

units.title: Transparency: pre-trade, post-trade, waivers, caps
objectives: Learner can explain why transparency exists and the main waivers to pre-trade transparency
Learner can describe the post-MiFIR-review regime (volume cap, deferrals, tape)
Learner can decide whether a trade is eligible for a waiver
key_concepts: waivers: reference price, negotiated, order management, large-in-scale
double volume cap replaced by single volume cap (2024 review)
units.worked_example: A 400,000 EUR block in a mid-cap trades via negotiated-trade waiver at the mid; it is reported post-trade within minutes while a large-in-scale deferral may delay publication of size.

exercises.task: Decide whether an order is large-in-scale for a given ADT threshold
Sort waiver types and their conditions
Place reporting events and deferral limits for a block trade
Spot the transparency breach in a venue rulebook excerpt

units.title: Dark trading, SIs and periodic auctions
objectives: Learner can explain how dark pools, midpoint crossing and periodic auctions differ
Learner can describe SI obligations and why SI internalisation matters for best execution
Learner can weigh information leakage vs price improvement
units.worked_example: A 200,000-share parent is sent first to a midpoint pool (rate of fill 4%), then to a periodic auction, and finally resting in the lit book; the learner compares expected impact for each leg.

exercises.task: Pick the venue type for a trading objective (size, urgency, leakage)
Compute price improvement from a midpoint fill vs lit touch
Match mechanisms (SI, periodic auction, midpoint, conditional) to descriptions
Select all true statements about SI duties

units.title: United States: Reg NMS and the NBBO world
objectives: Learner can explain NBBO, order protection and access rules
Learner can describe maker-taker pricing and its effects
Learner can compare EU and US routing duties
units.worked_example: A marketable order for 500 shares is routed to the venue showing the best protected quote; if another exchange has a better protected quote at that moment, trading through it is prohibited unless an exception applies.

exercises.task: Identify the NBBO and the venue the order must hit first
Compute net cost after maker-taker fees/rebates
Sequence a routing decision under order protection
Sort rules into EU vs US

sources.ref: Chapters on US market structure and fragmentation

units.title: Bonds and OTC: dealer markets and electronic platforms
objectives: Learner can explain why bonds are mostly OTC and dealer-based
Learner can compare voice, RFQ platforms and all-to-all venues
Learner can describe bond transparency and the EU consolidated tape for bonds
units.worked_example: A 5m EUR corporate bond block has ~3 quoting dealers; the investor sends an RFQ to 3 dealers on an MTF, receives 99.45, 99.42, 99.47 (clean) and hits the best offer - 5,000,000 x 99.42 plus accrued.

exercises.task: Choose the protocol for a bond order of given size and liquidity
Compute proceeds from the best of three dealer quotes incl. accrued

Sort instruments by dominant trading mechanism

sources.ref: Secondary market data and electronic trading papers

units.title: UK, Switzerland, Singapore, Hong Kong and a venue-chooser case
objectives: Learner can summarise the main structural differences of UK, CH, SG and HK markets
Learner can pick the right venue strategy for a cross-border order
Learner can compare tick-size and fee models
units.worked_example: A 120,000-share order in a Swiss large-cap is split between SIX lit and a local midpoint pool; the learner compares expected cost with the EU split of the same sized order across Xetra and a Cboe dark book.

exercises.task: Match regulatory regimes to key venue features
Select the best venue mix for an order
Spot the incorrect statement in a venue comparison table
Optional: compose a venue selection memo for a cross-border order

exercises.task: Identify the capacity of the firm in a scenario

exercises.task: Compute spread-capture P&L and mark-to-mid on a stream of trades

Learner can convert between price and yield quotation for a quote

exercises.task: Compute settlement amount incl. accrued from a clean price quote

units.title: Dealer execution across venues: SI, last look and conflicts

units.worked_example: Pre-hedging a 3m EUR client order ahead of an RFQ answer can reduce dealer risk but may harm the client if the market moves; ESMA warns it is permitted only when it serves the client and is disclosed.

modules.title: Best execution & TCA
modules.hook: The best-execution factors under MiFID II, execution policy, and transaction cost analysis against arrival price, VWAP and other benchmarks.

units.title: The best-execution duty: MiFID II Art 27
objectives: Learner can state the duty, its sufficient steps standard and who owes it
Learner can list the execution factors and how retail 'total consideration' differs
Learner can say where the duty does not apply
units.worked_example: A retail client's 5,000-share order: venue A gives 12.00 with 0.50 EUR commission, venue B gives 11.99 with 0.20 EUR fee; total consideration (price x quantity plus costs) shows which venue is cheaper.

exercises.task: Compute total consideration across two venues for a retail order

units.title: Execution policy, venue selection and monitoring

Learner can describe what replaced RTS 27/28 reporting after Directive 2024/790
units.worked_example: A firm's policy lists three venues for equities and an SI; the quarterly review finds that venue B's fill rate has dropped, so the policy committee proposes to demote it.

exercises.task: Identify the policy element missing from a sample policy

exercises.task: Pick the US rule that governs a stated fact pattern

units.title: Measuring cost: arrival, VWAP and implementation shortfall

Learner can compute implementation shortfall with explicit and implicit costs

units.worked_example: A PM decides to buy 100,000 at 20.00; the order arrives at 20.02, executes 80,000 at 20.08 average and 20,000 remain unfilled with the price at 20.20; IS = delay + impact + opportunity cost, computed in bps.

units.title: Commission worked cases
objectives: Compute brokerage under ad valorem, tiered and minimum-charge schedules
Apply an FX mark-up to a cross-currency trade and show it as a separate cost line

Detect a commission, tax or net-amount error on a contract note
key_concepts: Ad valorem commission as a percentage of notional
Tiered schedule: rate applies by band of notional
FX mark-up on the client rate vs market mid
Transaction taxes: French FTT 0.4% on in-scope French shares, Italian FTT 0.2% on regulated-market trades (see T6.2)
Net amount = notional +/- commission and fees +/- taxes (buy vs sell)
units.worked_example: A client buys 1,000 shares of a French listed company above EUR 1bn market cap at EUR 100.00: notional EUR 100,000. Tiered brokerage 0.30% on the first EUR 50,000 (150.00) and 0.15% on the rest (75.00) is EUR 225.00. French FTT 0.4% is EUR 400.00. Net debit EUR 100,625.00. For a small buy of 100 shares at EUR 12.00 (notional 1,200), 0.30% is 3.60, so the EUR 20 minimum applies. An FX-converted USD 10,000 purchase at mid 1.1000 with a 0.50% mark-up is quoted at 1.0945, costing EUR 9,136.59 vs EUR 9,090.91 at mid.

exercises.task: Compute tiered brokerage with minimum
Compute the FX mark-up cost
exercises.params: USD amount, mid rate, mark-up bp

exercises.task: Build the contract note cost lines to net amount

modules.jurisdiction_notes: EU (Art 59) and US (Rule 10b-10) side by side; no others.

modules.title: Calculus II
modules.hook: Definite integrals, the link between a rate and an accumulated amount, and Taylor expansions applied to the bond price-yield curve (convexity).

units.title: Accumulation: area under a curve and Riemann sums
objectives: Learner can approximate an area using left, right and midpoint sums
Learner can interpret area as accumulated quantity
Learner can write a sum in sigma notation
units.worked_example: Cash flow rate f(t)=100 EUR/year for 4 years: area = 400; with f(t)=50+25t, the right Riemann sum with 4 intervals is 50+75+100+125 = 350.

exercises.task: Compute a Riemann sum for a given function
Interpret the area in a context
Fill a table of left and right sums as n grows

units.title: Antiderivatives and the Fundamental Theorem
objectives: Learner can find simple antiderivatives
Learner can state the FTC and use it to evaluate definite integrals
Learner can check results by differentiating
units.worked_example: F(x)=x^3/3 is an antiderivative of x^2, so the integral from 1 to 3 is 27/3 - 1/3 = 26/3.

exercises.task: Evaluate a definite integral with FTC
Pick the correct antiderivative
Fill steps of an FTC computation

units.title: Integration rules and drills
objectives: Learner can integrate powers, exponentials, 1/x and sums
Learner can apply simple u-substitution
Learner can integrate by recognising derivative patterns
units.worked_example: Integral of 3e^{2x} dx = (3/2)e^{2x} + C; integral of 1/(x+1) dx = ln|x+1| + C.

exercises.task: Evaluate definite integrals from a function bank
Choose the substitution
Match integrands to antiderivatives
Spot the error in a worked integration

units.title: Integrals in finance: continuous cash flows and present value
objectives: Learner can compute total and present value of a continuous cash flow
Learner can connect integrals to annuity formulas
Learner can set up an integral from a word problem
units.worked_example: A stream paying 1,000 EUR/year for 5 years discounted continuously at 4% has PV = 1000 * (1 - e^{-0.2})/0.04 = 4,531.

exercises.task: Compute PV of a continuous stream
Set up the integral for a stated problem
Compare discrete annuity PV to the continuous limit

units.title: Exponential and logarithmic growth
objectives: Learner can solve y'=ky and interpret k
Learner can compute doubling times
Learner can link continuous growth to log returns
units.worked_example: At 3% continuous growth, wealth doubles in ln2/0.03 = 23.1 years.

exercises.task: Compute doubling time and growth for a rate
Pick the equation for a growth description
Fill the solution of y'=ky

units.title: Taylor approximation
objectives: Learner can build first- and second-order Taylor polynomials
Learner can estimate values using them
Learner can estimate the error roughly

exercises.task: Compute Taylor approximations to a function value
Fill the error table for increasing order
Choose the best order for a tolerance

units.title: Consolidation: derivatives and integrals together; bond price curve preview
objectives: Learner can combine derivatives and integrals in a problem
Learner can estimate price change from yield using first- and second-order terms
Learner can interpret the curve bend
units.worked_example: A bond price P(y)=100e^{-5y}; linear approximation at y=4% estimates the move for +50bp; adding the second-order term reduces the error.

exercises.task: Estimate price change from a yield move with first/second order
Identify the property from a curve
Optional: explain why linear approximation under-estimates a price gain

modules.unit_test: End-of-module test: integration technique, FTC, financial integral applications, growth and Taylor approximation.

modules.title: Probability II
modules.hook: Continuous distributions, the normal and lognormal models for returns, expectation and variance of sums, and covariance.

units.title: Random variables, expectation, variance
objectives: Learner can compute expectation and variance for discrete and simple continuous variables
Learner can apply linearity rules
Learner can interpret CDF and PDF
units.worked_example: Return X takes -5%, 0%, +8% with probabilities 0.2, 0.5, 0.3: E=1.4%, Var=22.24 (%-squared), sd about 4.7%

exercises.task: Compute E and Var of a discrete variable
Pick the CDF/PDF relation
Compute portfolio return mean and variance from linearity

units.title: The normal distribution
objectives: Learner can standardise and use z-scores
Learner can compute normal probabilities from tables
Learner can apply the 68-95-99.7 rule
units.worked_example: Monthly return ~ N(0.8%, 4%): P(return < -5%) = P(Z < -1.45) ~ 7.4%.

exercises.task: Compute a normal tail probability
Pick the interval for a given confidence
Find the quantile for a probability

units.title: Lognormal prices
objectives: Learner can explain why prices are modelled as lognormal
Learner can compute the mean and median of a lognormal
Learner can convert between log and simple returns

exercises.task: Compute lognormal mean and median
Choose the log vs simple return
Compute probability a price ends below a threshold

units.title: Law of large numbers and the CLT
objectives: Learner can state and use the CLT for sample means
Learner can compute standard error of an average return
Learner can explain where it fails (fat tails)
units.worked_example: With 60 monthly returns, sd 4%, SE = 0.52%; a 95% CI for mean return is +-1.0%.

exercises.task: Compute SE and a confidence interval
State when the CLT is reliable
Optional: explain why Sharpe estimates are noisy

modules.unit_test: End-of-module test: random variables, normal and lognormal probabilities, LLN/CLT and standard errors.

checkpoint: Level boss quiz (35-45 min) mixing all nine modules: an order-to-contract-note case (route, fills, cost, confirmation) plus calculus and probability items. Format: 25-30 mixed-template questions with 25% callbacks to L1-L2.
